 Order

This appeal by the claimant under section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act is arising out of the award dated 31.10.2017 passed by IInd MACT, Indore in Claim Case No.247/16 seeking enhancement of compensation amount awarded by the Tribunal.
2. The date of accident, negligence and the issue of liability are not in dispute and the findings recorded by the Tribunal in this regard are also not in question.

As per the findings of the Tribunal,
for the permanent disability suffered by the appellant, the Tribunal has awarded a total compensation of Rs.6,97,600/- along with interest.

The breakup of the compensation amount is as Ilumddin vs Motilal on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39747759/

 HEAD AMOUNT

Medical Bills -Rs.2,39,600/-

 Loss of income -Rs.9,000/-
 Special diet & transportation -Rs.11,000/-
 Artificial limb -Rs.50,000/-

Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the Tribunal has committed an error in not awarding just and proper amount of compensation in the case as the amount awarded by the Tribunal is on the lower side.
The appellant was working as blacksmith and used to earn Rs.20,000/- per month.
However, Tribunal committed an error in assessing the income of the injured as Rs.3000/- per month which deserves to be enhanced considering the minimum wages for the year 2016.
Tribunal has committed an error in assessing the permanent disability suffered by the appellant as 50% whereas treating doctor has opined 75% permanent disability.

No amount has been awarded by the Tribunal towards loss of future prospects keeping in view the law laid down by the apex Court in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi and others - 2017 ACJ 2700.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi and others - 2017 ACJ 2700
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The compensation awarded under other conventional heads is also on the lower side, hence prays for just and proper amount of compensation in the case.

4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the Insurance Company argued in support of the impugned award and contended that the Claims Tribunal has rightly awarded the compensation amount in the case which does not call for any interference by this Court.
5. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and going through the record, I find substance in the arguments advanced by the counsel for the appellant.

Firstly, I find that the income of the injured assessed by the Tribunal is on the lower side considering the minimum wages fixed by the Labour Department, Govt. of M.P for an unskilled labour in the year 2016, hence same is enhanced from Rs.3000/- to Rs.5500/-.
Secondly, the permanent disability calculated by the Tribunal is also on the lower side.

As per evidence that came on record appellant suffered multiple fracture in left lower limb with bone loss and vascular injuries and fracture in right mallolar bone which was operated and rod was inserved in right leg and left leg was operated and amputated from knee.
As per the PDC (Ex.P/13) he has suffered 75% permanent disability, therefore, considering all these evidence the permanent disability is fixed at 60%.

Thirdly, the Tribunal has not awarded any amount under the head of loss of future prospects in the light of the judgment of the apex Court in the case of Pranay Sethi (supra) for which he is entitled 40% amount as future prospects.

Considering the overall facts and circumstances of the case, the arguments advanced by the counsel for the parties and the evidence that came on record, in the considered opinion of this Court, the compensation Ilumddin vs Motilal on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39747759/
2 amount deserves to be enhanced as under:
 HEAD AMOUNT  Permanent disability -Rs.8,87,040/-
(i.e. Rs.5500 40% FP x 12 x16 (multiplier) x 60/100 (PDC)) Medical Bills -Rs.2,39,600/-
 Pain & suffering -Rs.25,000/-
 Loss of amenities -Rs.75,000/-
 Loss of income -Rs.16500/-
 Special diet & transportation -Rs.20,000/-
 Artificial limb -Rs.50,000/-
 --------------------

sentences.text: 6 . Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case is Rs.13,13,140/-, as against the award of the Tribunal of Rs.6,97,600/- .
Accordingly, the appellant is entitled to an additional sum of Rs.6,15,540/- over and above the amount which has been awarded by the Tribunal.
7. In the result, the appeal is partly allowed by enhancing the compensation amount by a sum of Rs.6,15,540/-.
The enhanced amount shall bear interest at the same rate as awarded by the Tribunal.
The other findings recorded by the Tribunal shall remain intact.

8. The appellant has valued the appeal only to the extent of Rs.6 lakhs and paid the Court fee accordingly, however, for the remaining amount, the Court fee shall be paid by the appellant within a period of one month and thereafter the amount shall be released by the Insurance Company on receiving the certificate.

In case the certificate has not been filed before the Insurance Company up to a period of three months, the claimant shall not be entitled to receive the interest on the enhanced amount of compensation.
9. In the result, the appeal is allowed in part and to the extent indicated herein above.

(HIRDESH) JUDGE hk/
